description: Join Prospect Park Alliance this fall to help spruce up the park after a busy summer season. Join a Fall Fix Up event on September 30; October 7, 14, 21, or 28; or November 4, 12, 18, or 25. Please note that locations vary by date. Appropriate for adults only. title: Prospect Park Stroller Walk
description: Calling all parents and caregivers with children! Join a Prospect Park Alliance Naturalist for a leisurely stroll along Prospect Park’s waterways. Embrace the sound of streams and songs of birds, while enjoying fragrant flowers and the towering trees of Brooklyn’s Backyard. Please note that this walk leaves promptly at 10 am from the Prospect Park Boathouse. RSVP to reserve your spot: RSVP Please check your email prior to the event for changes, updates and to confirm the walk has met a minimum participant requirement

title: Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit
description: Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

title: October Weekday Nature Exploration
description: Join Prospect Park Alliance for nature education programs on Thursdays and Fridays at the Prospect Park Audubon Center, the first urban Audubon Center in the nation. Leaf Art, 10 am –3 pm: Let’s have fun exploring the unique features of trees and their uniquely shaped leaves. Let your creativity flourish as you craft art inspired by nature. Nature Detective, 10 am–3 pm: What can you discover when you slow down and look closely? Borrow a sketchbook and observation guide, then record your discoveries and sketch what catches your eye, just like a naturalist in the field! Fall Leaf Discovery, 2–3 pm: Join us as we delve into the wonder of nature! Are you curious about why and when trees shed their leaves? Gain hands-on experience in citizen science as we explore the Prospect Park environment and witness how changing temperatures affect the trees. We will provide you with a guide to help you record your observations. This program leaves the Audubon Center promptly at 2 pm.

title: Alfreda's Cinema, Ten Minutes to Live (1932) w/ Live Vinyl Score
description: Join Prospect Park Alliance and Alfreda’s Cinema for the 2026 Open-Air Film Sessions, where Black stories breathe under open skies. Experience Oscar Micheaux’s classic 1932 mystery-thriller, Ten Minutes to Live, transformed by a live vinyl score curated to amplify every twist, turn, and rhythm of Harlem’s historic screen legacy. Bring a blanket and settle in for an unforgettable night of cinema, music, and community in Prospect Park. RSVP

title: Greenmarket at Grand Army Plaza
description: At what other market can you do all your food shopping, sample local wine and explore Brooklyn’s favorite park? Established in 1989, the Grand Army Plaza greenmarket is the flagship Brooklyn market. EBT/Food Stamps and WIC & Senior FMNP coupons accepted year-round. Learn More For a full calendar of events and a list of sellers, visit the GrowNYC website. Learn about all Nutrition Benefit Programs accepted at GrowNYC Markets.

title: Dance Fitness with Shape Up NYC at the Boathouse
description: Join Prospect Park Alliance and Shape-up NYC for a fun-filled dance fitness zumba class at the Boathouse! Zumba is a fusion of Latin, International and popular music dance themes creating a dynamic, exciting, effective fitness system. All levels are welcomed and encouraged. Whether you want to learn some new choreography or need a space to step-touch and sing, this class is for you!

title: Introduction to Birdwatching Outings
description: Whether you’re new to birding or looking to build your skills, this introductory outing is a great way to explore Prospect Park and learn about the birds that visit throughout the year. Join a member of the Brooklyn Bird Club to learn birding basics and search for the dozens of species found in the park across all seasons. All ages and experience levels are welcome. No registration is required. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. What to Bring: Binoculars if you have them, comfortable walking shoes, water, and weather-appropriate clothing. A limited number of binoculars will be available to borrow. Please Note: Pets are not permitted on this outing. Depending on attendance, participants may be divided into smaller groups. Outings are held rain or shine unless severe weather makes conditions unsafe. Route Description: This outing moves at a relaxed pace with frequent stops to observe birds. Routes may vary from week to week depending on bird activity and park conditions. Participants can expect paved paths, dirt trails, grassy areas, slight inclines and occasional steps. The group will cover approximately 1.5–2 miles. Learn more on the Brooklyn Bird Club website.

title: Creepy Crawly Halloween
description: Take a second look at the creatures that give you the creeps, you may find you like them! Participate in fun activities and experiments that will make your spine tingle at Prospect Park Alliance’s Creepy Crawly Halloween. Nature Detective, 10 am–4 pm What creepy, crawly and curious creatures are hiding in Prospect Park? Borrow a sketchbook and observation guide, then explore indoors and outdoors for spiders, bats, insects, plants, and other wild discoveries. Look closely, sketch what you find, and uncover the mysteries of nature hiding all around you. Owl Pellet Dissection, 11 am–2pm Participants will have the opportunity to pick apart owl pellets, masses of undigested parts of food that owl species occasionally regurgitate! Nature Chef’s Surprise!, 12–3 pm Our nature chef has some tasty treats for you to try that are delicious, nutritious, and crunchy! Take a nibble and earn a special certificate and boasting button. Learn how this mystery treat is a sustainable alternative protein source that has nutritional benefits. Creepy Crawly Walk, 1–2 pm + 3–4pm Participants will search for Prospect Park’s creepy residents and explore the park.

title: Spooktober! At Prospect Park Zoo
description: Go batty every weekend in October at the Prospect Park Zoo! Visit the tombstones of extinct animals in Sea Lion Court and learn why extinction isn’t inevitable with your help. Our Spooky Trail will show you some of our “spooky” neighbors who come out at night. Discover some Spooky Science and enjoy special live performances. Come in costume and take a photo at one of our beautiful harvest decoration areas. Learn more at the Prospect Park Zoo website.

title: Park Pitch In: Nethermead Care
description: Join Prospect Park Alliance to help beautify the Nethermead. Located in the heart of the park, the Nethermead is a rolling meadow where the sights and sounds of the city fade away. Volunteers will be mulching, clearing pathways, and removing unwanted plants. Appropriate for groups, teens and adults. Register as an Individual or Register as a Group Register online or call (929) 888-6826 for more information.

title: Pop-Up Audubon I
description: Celebrate Autumn in Prospect Park by supporting migratory birds! Join Prospect Park Alliance Naturalists to design your own colorful autumn leaf window cling. These fun, decorative clings help prevent bird-window collisions by making glass more visible to migrating birds. All materials provided — family-friendly and free to participate! Also enjoy: Stay + Play, 12–3 pm: Families, children and caregivers can enjoy a range of nature fun including games, puzzles and drawing activities. Nature on the Go, 3–4 pm: Join an Alliance Naturalist as we explore the park’s trails for signs of fall. Be a Park Champion by helping pick up trash along the way. Pop-Up Audubon will be canceled in the event of inclement weather, including rain, extreme heat (temperatures of 90°F or higher), or “Very Unhealthy” air quality conditions.

title: Pop-Up Audubon II
description: Have you ever wondered what lives beneath your feet on the forest floor? Join Prospect Park Alliance naturalists to explore the hidden world of leaf litter. Through hands-on observation, you’ll uncover insects, decomposers, and other small creatures that play a big role in keeping the ecosystem healthy. Also enjoy: Stay + Play, 12–3 pm: Families, children and caregivers can enjoy a range of nature fun including games, puzzles and drawing activities. Nature on the Go, 3–4 pm: Join an Alliance Naturalist as we explore the park’s trails for signs of fall. Be a Park Champion by helping pick up trash along the way. Pop-Up Audubon will be canceled in the event of inclement weather, including rain, extreme heat (temperatures of 90°F or higher), or “Very Unhealthy” air quality conditions.

title: Exhibit: The Shirley Chisholm Way: Brooklyn's Blueprint for Change
description: Join Prospect Park Alliance and Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute (SCCI) for a new exhibit that explores how Brooklyn’s beloved daughter broke down gender and racial barriers to fight for her community, becoming the first Black woman elected to Congress. The exhibit is organized around seven life lessons drawn from Chisholm’s tenacious career. It features stunning portraits of Chisholm by artist Al Johnson and rarely seen photographs and memorabilia from the Congresswoman’s campaigns, curated by Barbara Bullard, Creative Producer and President of SCCI. These materials offer inspirational insights into how Brooklyn’s beloved daughter broke down gender and racial barriers to become the first Black woman to serve in Congress. This exhibit provides visitors with a space to reflect on Chisholm’s legacy as Prospect Park Alliance welcomes the installation of a new monument in her honor at the Parkside and Ocean Avenue entrance in 2027. The exhibit, curated by Barbara Bullard, Cultural Producer and President of the Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute, is part of Prospect Park Alliance’s ReImagine Lefferts initiative, which is transforming the museum to explore the legacies of resistance and resilience of the Indigenous people of Lenapehoking, whose unceded ancestral lands the park and house rests upon, and Africans who were enslaved by the Lefferts family. The Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute (SCCI) has been at the forefront of art, culture, and justice and economic sustainability since 1977, with the official permission and participation of Congresswoman Chisholm herself in its inception and development. Its purpose is to preserve the legacy of Congresswoman Shirley Chisholm through the initiatives cultivated during her public service career with 21st century activism and innovation. SCCI is aligned with grassroots groups and frontline communities through creating substantive community-based partnership and collaboration along with strategic interoperative relationships with leaders of governmental, and mainstream organizations.

description: Gather at the Washington Irving statue and join the Urban Park Rangers for a hike learning about the folklore and history surrounding Sleepy Hollow while enjoying a nature walk through Prospect Park.
